arxiv-1808-02558.title: Tensor Train accelerated solvers for nonsmooth rigid body dynamics
arxiv-1808-02558.creator: Eduardo Corona, David Gorsich, Paramsothy Jayakumar and Shravan Veerapaneni
arxiv-1808-02558.description: Abstract In the last two decades, increased need for high-fidelity simulations of the time evolution and propagation of forces in granular media has spurred a renewed interest in the discrete element method (DEM) modeling of frictional contact. Force penalty methods, while economic and widely accessible, introduce artificial stiffness, requiring small time steps to retain numerical stability.

arxiv-2204-11962.title: On bounded ratios of minors of totally positive matrices
arxiv-2204-11962.creator: DANIEL SOSKIN, MICHAEL GEKHTMAN
arxiv-2204-11962.description: Abstract . We construct several examples of bounded Laurent monomials in minors of an n × n n\times n totally positive matrix, which can not be factored into a product of so called primitive bounded ratios thus disproving the conjecture about factorization of bounded ratios stated in [ 7 ] by Fallat, Gekhtman, and Johnson.

arxiv-2210-12883.title: A Greek Parliament Proceedings Dataset for Computational Linguistics and Political Analysis
arxiv-2210-12883.creator: Konstantina Dritsa, Kaiti Thoma, John Pavlopoulos, Panos Louridas
arxiv-2210-12883.description: Abstract Large, diachronic datasets of political discourse are hard to come across, especially for resource-lean languages such as g In this paper, we introduce a curated dataset of the Greek Parliament Proceedings that extends chronologically from 1989 up to 2020. It consists of more than 1 million speeches with extensive metadata, extracted from 5,355 parliamentary record files.

arxiv-2211-09420.title: Mediation analysis with case-control sampling: Identification and estimation in the presence of a binary mediator
arxiv-2211-09420.creator: Marco Doretti, Minna Genbäck, Elena Stanghellini
arxiv-2211-09420.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marco Doretti, Minna Genbäck, Elena Stanghellini. With reference to a stratified case-control procedure based on a binary variable of primary interest, we derive the expression of the distortion induced by the sampling design on the parameters of the logistic model of a secondary variable. This is particularly relevant when performing mediation analysis (possibly in a causal framework) with stratified case-control data in settings where both the outcome and the mediator are binary. Our identification result opens the way to M-estimation and Maximum Likelihood estimation.

arxiv-2301-01088.title: Explaining Imitation Learning through Frames
arxiv-2301-01088.creator: Boyuan Zheng, Jianlong ZhouChunjie Liu, Yiqiao Li, Fang Chen
arxiv-2301-01088.description: Abstract As one of the prevalent methods to achieve automation systems, Imitation Learning (IL) presents a promising performance in a wide range of domains. However, despite the considerable improvement in policy performance, the corresponding research on the explainability of IL models is still limited.

arxiv-2311-09436.title: A characterization of piecewise ℱ \mathcal{F} -syndetic sets
arxiv-2311-09436.creator: Conner Griffin
arxiv-2311-09436.description: Abstract Some filter relative notions of size, ( ℱ , 𝒢 ) \left(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\right) -syndeticity and piecewise ℱ \mathcal{F} -syndeticity, were defined and applied with clarity and focus by Shuungula, Zelenyuk and Zelenyuk Shuungula et al. 2009 . These notions are generalizations of the well studied notions of syndeticity and piecewise syndeticity.

arxiv-2403-16489.title: Spatially temporally distributed informative path planning for multi-robot systems
arxiv-2403-16489.creator: Binh Nguyen, Linh Nguyen, Truong X. Nghiem, Hung La, José Baca, Pablo Rangel, Miguel Cid Montoya, Thang Nguyen
arxiv-2403-16489.description: Abstract This paper investigates the problem of informative path planning for a mobile robotic sensor network in spatially temporally distributed mapping. The robots are able to gather noisy measurements from an area of interest during their movements to build a Gaussian Process (GP) model of a spatio-temporal field.

arxiv-2405-03081.title: Design optimization in unilateral contact using pressure constraints and Bayesian optimization
arxiv-2405-03081.creator: Jingyi Wang, Jerome Solberg, Mike A. Puso, Eric B. Chin, Cosmin G. Petra
arxiv-2405-03081.description: Abstract Design optimization problems, e.g. , shape optimization, that involve deformable bodies in unilateral contact are challenging as they require robust contact solvers, complex optimization methods that are typically gradient-based, and sensitivity derivations. Notably, the problems are nonsmooth, adding significant difficulty to the optimization process.

arxiv-2406-04069.title: Hyperbolicity of smooth logarithmic and orbifold pairs in ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n}
arxiv-2406-04069.creator: Clara Dérand
arxiv-2406-04069.description: Abstract We derive a necessary and sufficient condition on a hyperplane arrangement in ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} for the associated logarithmic cotangent bundle to be ample modulo boundary. We extend this result to the orbifold setting and give some applications concerning hyperbolicity of pairs. We improve significantly the results of [ 11 ] . 1 Introduction 1.

arxiv-2601-04572.title: Spatial-Temporal Feedback Diffusion Guidance for Controlled Traffic Imputation
arxiv-2601-04572.creator: Xiaowei Mao, Huihu Ding, Yan Lin, Tingrui Wu, Shengnan Guo, Dazhuo Qiu, Feiling Fang, Jilin Hu, Huaiyu Wan
arxiv-2601-04572.description: Abstract Imputing missing values in spatial-temporal traffic data is essential for intelligent transportation systems. Among advanced imputation methods, score-based diffusion models have demonstrated competitive performance. These models generate data by reversing a noising process, using observed values as conditional guidance.

arxiv-2601-10649.title: CURVE : A Benchmark for Cultural and Multilingual Long Video Reasoning
arxiv-2601-10649.creator: Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari, Tobias Weyand, Cordelia Schmid, Anelia Angelova, Shachi Dave
arxiv-2601-10649.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari, Tobias Weyand, Cordelia Schmid, Anelia Angelova, Shachi Dave. Recent advancements in video models have shown tremendous progress, particularly in long video understanding. However, current benchmarks predominantly feature western-centric data and English as the dominant language, introducing significant biases in evaluation. To address this, we introduce CURVE ( C ultural U nderstanding and R easoning in V ideo E valuation), a challenging benchmark for multicultural and multilingual video reasoning.

arxiv-2601-21450.title: Variance & GREEDINESS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF METRIC-LEARNING LOSSES
arxiv-2601-21450.creator: Donghuo Zeng, Hao Niu, Zhi Li, Masato Taya
arxiv-2601-21450.description: Abstract Metric learning is central to retrieval, yet its effects on embedding geometry and optimization dynamics are not well understood. We introduce a diagnostic framework, VARIANCE (intra-/inter-class variance) and GREEDINESS (active ratio and gradient norms), to compare seven representative losses, i.e., Contrastive, Triplet, N-pair, InfoNCE, ArcFace, SCL, and CCL, across five image-retrieval datasets.

britannica-1911-huntington-west-virginia.title: Huntington (West Virginia) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-huntington-west-virginia.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-huntington-west-virginia.description: Article 'Huntington (West Virginia)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 13), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. West Virginia, U.S.A., about 50 m. bank of the Ohio river, just below the mouth of the Guyandotte river. (1900) 11,923, of whom 1212 were negroes; (1910 census) 31,161. It is served by the Baltimore & Ohio and the Chesapeake & Ohio railways, and by several lines of river steamboats.

europmc-pmc1570152.title: Tools for integrated sequence-structure analysis with UCSF Chimera.
europmc-pmc1570152.creator: Meng EC, Pettersen EF, Couch GS, Huang CC, Ferrin TE.
europmc-pmc1570152.description: Background Comparing related structures and viewing the structures in the context of sequence alignments are important tasks in protein structure-function research. While many programs exist for individual aspects of such work, there is a need for interactive visualization tools

europmc-pmc2707010.title: The PRISMA statement for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses of studies that evaluate health care interventions: explanation and elaboration.
europmc-pmc2707010.creator: Liberati A, Altman DG, Tetzlaff J, Mulrow C, Gøtzsche PC, Ioannidis JP, Clarke M, Devereaux PJ, Kleijnen J, Moher D.
europmc-pmc2707010.description: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses are essential to summarize evidence relating to efficacy and safety of health care interventions accurately and reliably. The clarity and transparency of these reports, however, is not optimal. Poor reporting of systematic reviews diminishes...

europmc-pmc4737895.title: Rapid endothelial cytoskeletal reorganization enables early blood-brain barrier disruption and long-term ischaemic reperfusion brain injury.
europmc-pmc4737895.creator: Shi Y, Zhang L, Pu H, Mao L, Hu X, Jiang X, Xu N, Stetler RA, Zhang F, Liu X, Leak RK, Keep RF, Ji X, Chen J.
europmc-pmc4737895.description: The mechanism and long-term consequences of early blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption after cerebral ischaemic/reperfusion (I/R) injury are poorly understood. Here we discover that I/R induces subtle BBB leakage within 30-60 min, likely independent of gelatinase B/MMP-9...

pmc-10504240.title: First fully-automated AI/ML virtual screening cascade implemented at a drug discovery centre in Africa
pmc-10504240.creator: Gemma Turon, Jason Hlozek, John G Woodland, Ankur Kumar, Kelly Chibale, Miquel Duran-Frigola
pmc-10504240.description: Streamlined data-driven drug discovery remains challenging, especially in resource-limited settings. We present ZairaChem, an artificial intelligence (AI)- and machine learning (ML)-based tool for quantitative structure-activity/property relationship (QSAR/QSPR) modelling. ZairaChem is fully automated, requires low computational resources and works across a broad spectrum of datasets.

pmc-10635748.title: A Case of Syphilis Suspected Preoperatively as a Case of Tongue Cancer
pmc-10635748.creator: Shigeru Kondo, Ryuhei Okada, Yosuke Ariizumi, Takashi Kurita, Hiroshi Shintaku, Takahiro Asakage
pmc-10635748.description: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by Treponema pallidum (TP). We report a case of syphilis that was initially suspected as tongue cancer. An 86-year-old man consulted a neighborhood clinic with an approximately one-month history of pain in the right tongue.

pmc-10648533.title: Studying Fluorescence Sensing of Acetone and Tryptophan and Antibacterial Properties Based on Zinc-Based Triple Interpenetrating Metal–Organic Skeletons
pmc-10648533.creator: Congying Yuan, Yidan Qiao, Zhaolei Zhang, Yinhang Chai, Xiaojun Zhang, Xiaojing Dong, Ying Zhao, Takahiro Kusukawa
pmc-10648533.description: Two triple interpenetrating Zn(II)-based MOFs were studied in this paper. Named [Zn6(1,4-bpeb)4(IPA)6(H2O)]n (MOF-1) and {[Zn3(1,4-bpeb)1.5(DDBA)3]n·2DMF} (MOF-2), {1,4-bpeb = 1,4-bis [2-(4-pyridy1) ethenyl]benze, IPA = Isophthalic acid, DDBA = 3,3′-Azodibenzoic acid}, they were synthesized by the hydrothermal method and were characterized and stability tested. The results showed that MOF-1 had good acid–base stability and solvent stability.

pmc-11595856.title: Challenges and Performance of Filter Dusts as a Supplementary Cementitious Material
pmc-11595856.creator: Johannes Berger, Anabella Mocciaro, Gisela Cordoba, Cecilia Martinefsky, Edgardo F Irassar, Nancy Beuntner, Sebastian Scherb, Karl-Christian Thienel, Alejandra Tironi, Paweł Strzałkowski, Ekin Köken, Luís M O Sousa
pmc-11595856.description: Global industry relies on a linear approach for economic growth. One step towards transformation is the implementation of a circular economy and the reclamation of anthropogenic deposits. This study examines two filter dusts, one German and one Argentinian, from the production of calcined clays, representing such deposits.

pmc-12528415.title: Plastome phylogenomics of the Korean endemic plant Arisaema thunbergii subsp. geomundoense (Araceae)
pmc-12528415.creator: Joonhyung Jung, Suvin Seok, Hye One Kim, Kashish Kamra, Hyuk-Jin Kim, Joo-Hwan Kim
pmc-12528415.description: Studying endemic plants is crucial for enhancing biodiversity in their unique habitats and exploring their evolutionary history. However, classification relying only on morphological traits can be subjective and may lead to inconsistencies in taxonomy. To address this issue, molecular approaches are necessary for precise identification and classification. The Korean endemic plant Arisaema thunbergii Blume subsp. geomundoense S.C.Ko (Araceae Juss.

pmc-12641143.title: Knowledge of Obstetric Fistula and Its Associated Factors Among Women of Childbearing Age in Buno Bedele Zone, Southwest Ethiopia: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-12641143.creator: Bashatu Berkessa Tola, Gizachew Abdissa Bulto, Eden Girmaye Tefera, Fikadu Wondimu Abdissa
pmc-12641143.description: Background and AimsObstetric fistulas are one of the most serious and catastrophic complications that occur during childbirth. Increasing awareness among women may contribute positively to its reduction and prompt treatment initiation. Although limited studies have been conducted on the knowledge of obstetric fistulas, they were mainly conducted among women who sought care at health institutions.

pmc-13062154.title: Federated multi-label text feature selection via manifold-aware sparse modeling and cooperative grey wolf optimization
pmc-13062154.creator: Yufeng Zheng, Zhiwei Ye, Songsong Zhang, Kaiqi Wang
pmc-13062154.description: Feature selection (FS) for multi-label text classification faces issues such as high dimensionality, strong label correlations, and sparse features, which often lead to suboptimal feature subsets. Moreover, most existing methods are centralized and thus ill-suited to real-world distributed or federated settings, where text data are scattered across multiple nodes and effective FS mechanisms are lacking.

pmc-13396291.title: Current clinical applications and clinical evidence of Bojungikki-tang, a traditional East Asian multi-botanical preparation: a scoping review
pmc-13396291.creator: Soo-Dam Kim, Boram Lee, Yang-Chun Park, Yee Ran Lyu
pmc-13396291.description: BackgroundBojungikki-tang (Buzhongyiqi decoction, Hochuekkito, BIT) has been used in East Asian medicine for conditions with fatigue, reduced appetite, and functional decline. In recent years, research on this preparation has expanded across diverse disease areas, yet its contemporary evidence landscape has not been systematically mapped.
